text:
Brock Boeser became the eighth Canucks player to reach 500 points last week, and he keeps rolling: an eight-game point streak, 23 points in 23 games, and a bump to nearly 21 minutes a night over his last ten. Fourteen of those points have come on the power play, where he remains Vancouver's trigger man.

Our numbers like the role and doubt the rate. He has eight goals on 5.4 expected goals (the quality of his chances), shooting 22% after 13% last season, and the Canucks have scored 5.7 more goals than expected with him on the ice. His 3.09 points per 60 sits well above our range for him (about 2.3 in the middle). That flags him as due to cool, not as a fraud: the shot is still elite, with EDGE putting his top shot speed in the 91st percentile.

The worry is the other end. At 5v5 Vancouver gets only 35.8% of the expected goals with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with chances against piling up. Vancouver Hockey Daily already asked what his pace means for his future with the club. Finishing will decide how loud that question gets.
